sections.title: What does end-to-end mean?
lecture_lines: End-to-end describes how information moves through a driving system.
First, compare it with the traditional modular approach.
animations: Set up a comparison between explicit modules and one learned system.

sections.title: Traditional modular pipeline
lecture_lines: Planning chooses a route, then control steers and brakes.
animations: Connect camera, perception, planning, and control with arrows.

sections.title: Each module has one job
lecture_lines: Perception labels lanes, cars, and pedestrians.
Planning converts those labels into a safe path.
animations: Reveal labeled road objects, then transform them into a route.

sections.title: The end-to-end alternative
lecture_lines: One neural network learns camera pixels to driving actions.
Hand-designed boundaries become learned internal representations.
animations: Collapse the separate modules into one neural-network block.

sections.title: How the network learns
lecture_lines: Training examples pair road scenes with expert steering and braking.
The network adjusts until its actions match those demonstrations.
animations: Flow from demonstrations through training into a learned model.

sections.title: The essential contrast
lecture_lines: End-to-end systems learn the full camera-to-control relationship.
animations: Finish with a side-by-side comparison and highlight the learned path.
